en: Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it.
Lower the bar to mid-chest with elbows about 45° from your body.
Press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell on each thigh, then lie back.
Hold the dumbbells above your chest, palms facing forward.
Lower them slowly to chest level.
Press them up and slightly together.
Set the bench to about 30°.
Hold the dumbbells at upper-chest level.
Press them up until your arms are straight.
Lower under control.
Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor.
Keep your hips in line with your shoulders.
Push back up to straight arms.
Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders.
Keep a straight line from knees to head.
Lower your chest towards the floor.
Push back up.
Set both pulleys at shoulder height and step forward.
With a slight bend in the elbows, open your arms wide.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Return slowly.
Hang from the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your chest towards the bar, leading with the elbows.
Get your chin over the bar.
Lower all the way down with control.
Sit with thighs under the pads and grip the bar wide.
Lean back slightly and pull the bar to your upper chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Let the bar rise slowly.
Sit tall with knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle to your stomach, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades.
Extend your arms slowly.
Place one knee and hand on a bench, back flat.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand, arm straight.
Pull it towards your hip.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch sides.
Stand with the bar over mid-foot, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Brace your core, flatten your back, and stand up by pushing the floor away.
Lower the bar by hinging at the hips first.
Anchor the band at chest height.
Hold the ends and step back until there is tension.
Pull your hands to your ribs.
Return slowly.
Hold the bar at shoulder height, grip just outside your shoulders.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar straight overhead.
Lower it back to your shoulders.
Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press them overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly to shoulder level.
Stand with dumbbells at your sides.
With a slight bend in the elbows, raise your arms out to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
Stand holding the bar with palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Curl the bar towards your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Curl them up without swinging.
Squeeze at the top and lower slowly.
Hold the bar or rope at chest height, elbows by your sides.
Push down until your arms are straight.
Return slowly without moving your elbows.
Sit on a bench edge with hands next to your hips.
Slide forward so you are supported by your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower your body.
Push back up.
Rest the bar on your upper back, feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and sit down between your heels.
Go down until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive back up through your whole foot.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest.
Squat down keeping your chest up.
Push your knees out over your toes.
Stand back up.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms forward.
Sit back and down as if onto a chair.
Keep your heels on the floor.
Stand back up.
Sit with your back flat against the pad, feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Lower the platform until your knees are at about 90°.
Push it back without locking your knees.
Step forward and lower until both knees are at about 90°.
Keep your front knee over your ankle.
Push off and step into the next lunge.
Hold the bar at hip height, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and lower the bar along your legs.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to stand up.
Sit with your upper back against a bench and the bar over your hips.
Plant your feet hip-width apart.
Drive your hips up until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Lower slowly.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Push through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower slowly.
Stand on the edge of a step with heels hanging off.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can.
Lower your heels below the step.
Rest on your forearms and toes.
Keep a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and hold without letting your hips sag.
Stand with feet wider than hips, kettlebell in both hands.
Hinge at the hips and swing the bell between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing it to chest height.
Let it fall back and repeat.
